title: Normalized tensor extension of compatible torsion line systems
statement:
Let $h:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, with small pro-etale sites and inverse image $h^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix a prime $\ell$. For a finite commutative ring $A$ let $A_T$ be its constant ring sheaf on $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and let $\gamma_A:h^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X$ be the constant-section comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Suppose $P_{T,r}$, $r\ge1$, are sheaves of $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with semilinear transitions $q^T_{s,r}:P_{T,s}\to P_{T,r}$ for $s\ge r$, with identities and composition. Assume the induced maps
$$P_{T,s}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^s)_T}(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T\longrightarrow P_{T,r}$$
are isomorphisms. Suppose isomorphisms $c_r:h^{-1}P_{Y,r}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{X,r}$ are semilinear over $\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ and satisfy $c_rh^{-1}q^Y_{s,r}=q^X_{s,r}c_s$.
For every finite commutative $A$ with $\ell^rA=0$, set $P_T(A;r)=P_{T,r}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T}A_T$, using sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There is a unique $\gamma_A$-semilinear isomorphism
$$C_{A,r}:h^{-1}P_Y(A;r)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_X(A;r)$$
sending every local pure tensor $h^{-1}(x\otimes a)$ to $c_r(h^{-1}x)\otimes\gamma_A(h^{-1}a)$. These maps commute with every coefficient homomorphism $A\to B$ for which $\ell^rA=\ell^rB=0$ and every exponent-change map induced by $q_{s,r}$, including the canonical isomorphism $P_T(A;s)\cong P_T(A;r)$ when $\ell^rA=0$. More generally, they commute with any transition $(s,A)\to(r,B)$ defined by $s\ge r$, a ring homomorphism $A\to B$, $\ell^sA=0$, $\ell^rB=0$, and the formula $x\otimes a\mapsto q_{s,r}(x)\otimes\bar a$. Thus they give an isomorphism of the resulting diagrams of module sheaves with varying scalar rings. Interpreting these modules as internal module objects via [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and its tensor comparison [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] gives the same maps on underlying abelian sheaves.

proof.text: Write $R_{T,r}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T$, and write $[x]=h^{-1}x$ for the inverse-image unit section over $X\times_YV$ of a section $x$ over $V$. Every unital coefficient homomorphism $v:A\to B$ commutes with the canonical maps from $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ whenever both rings are annihilated by $\ell^r$. Moreover $v_X\gamma_A=\gamma_Bh^{-1}v_Y$: under the ring adjunction these maps are the maps $A_Y\to h_*B_X$ sending a constant section $a$ to the constant section $v(a)$. They agree by the constant-presheaf sheafification universal property. This also proves compatibility of $\gamma_A$ with $R_{Y,r}\to A_Y$, and with every reduction $R_{Y,s}\to R_{Y,r}$. Thus the scalar identifications below are compatible ring-sheaf identifications, rather than choices of abstract isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text:
Apply clause 1 of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] with $\mathcal O=R_{Y,r}$, $\mathcal F=P_{Y,r}$ and $\mathcal G=A_Y$. Its isomorphism is followed by the map on tensors induced by $c_r$ and $\gamma_A$:
$$h^{-1}(P_{Y,r}\otimes_{R_{Y,r}}A_Y)\xrightarrow{\sigma}h^{-1}P_{Y,r}\otimes_{h^{-1}R_{Y,r}}h^{-1}A_Y\xrightarrow{c_r\otimes\gamma_A}P_{X,r}\otimes_{R_{X,r}}A_X.$$
The second arrow is defined by the balanced-bilinear universal property, using the scalar square in step 1 and the assumed semilinearity of $c_r$. Its inverse is induced by $c_r^{-1}$ and $\gamma_A^{-1}$; both composites fix pure tensors, so are identities by that same universal property. This constructs $C_{A,r}$ as an isomorphism. Multiplication by a section $b$ of $h^{-1}A_Y$ acts on the second tensor factor; the displayed map changes it to multiplication by $\gamma_A(b)$. Hence $C_{A,r}$ is $\gamma_A$-semilinear, with exactly the required formula $[x\otimes a]\mapsto c_r([x])\otimes\gamma_A([a])$.

proof.text: Here is the equality test used for uniqueness and all later squares. For maps from $h^{-1}(P_{Y,s}\otimes_{R_{Y,s}}A_Y)$ to an abelian sheaf $H$ on $X$, take adjuncts to maps $P_{Y,s}\otimes_{R_{Y,s}}A_Y\to h_*H$. In the semilinear situation give $h_*H$ the $R_{Y,s}$-action through the specified coefficient map and the constant-section structure map. The adjuncts are then $R_{Y,s}$-linear. The tensor universal property says they agree if they agree on $x\otimes a$ over every $V$. By naturality of the adjunction unit this is precisely agreement of the original maps on all $[x\otimes a]$. Apply this test with $s=r$ and $H=P_X(A;r)$: any semilinear map with the prescribed formula equals the map constructed in step 2. This proves the asserted uniqueness without assuming that arbitrary inverse-image sections are single unit sections.

proof.text: For an allowed transition $v:(s,A)\to(r,B)$ define $D_T(v)$ on pure tensors by $x\otimes a\mapsto q^T_{s,r}(x)\otimes v_T(a)$. For a local section $b$ of $R_{T,s}$, semilinearity of $q^T_{s,r}$ gives $q^T_{s,r}(bx)=\bar bq^T_{s,r}(x)$, while the unital ring map gives $v_T(ba)=\bar b v_T(a)$. Thus the formula is balanced and biadditive. The tensor universal property, with the target viewed as an $R_{T,s}$-module, defines the map of sheaves. It is semilinear over $v_T$ by multiplication on the second factor. Identities act as $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes a$; composing transitions sends $x\otimes a$ to $q^T_{r,t}q^T_{s,r}(x)\otimes w_Tv_T(a)=q^T_{s,t}(x)\otimes(wv)_T(a)$. Tensor uniqueness proves the diagram laws. This includes coefficient-only and exponent-only transitions.

proof.text:
Fix $s\ge r$ and $\ell^rA=0$. There is an elementary tensor reassociation
$$P_{T,s}\otimes_{R_{T,s}}A_T\cong(P_{T,s}\otimes_{R_{T,s}}R_{T,r})\otimes_{R_{T,r}}A_T.$$
Explicitly the forward map sends $x\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes a$, and the reverse sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$ to $x\otimes ba$. Each is well defined by the balanced-bilinear universal property, applied twice on the right. The composites fix $x\otimes a$ and $(x\otimes b)\otimes a$, respectively: $(x\otimes1)\otimes ba=(x\otimes b)\otimes a$. These identities prove they are inverse, as sheaf maps, without identifying tensor-sheaf sections with sectionwise tensors.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text: Follow step 5's forward isomorphism by $\bar q^T_{s,r}\otimes1$, where $\bar q^T_{s,r}:P_{T,s}\otimes_{R_{T,s}}R_{T,r}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{T,r}$ is an isomorphism by the hypothesis of the item. Tensoring it with $A_T$ is invertible: tensor its inverse to obtain an inverse map, with composites equal to the identity on pure tensors. The resulting isomorphism $P_T(A;s)\to P_T(A;r)$ sends $x\otimes a$ to $q^T_{s,r}(x)\otimes a$, so is exactly $D_T((s,A)\to(r,A))$ from step 4. Thus exponent independence concerns the specified transition, with no arbitrary choice of identifications.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text:
For every allowed $v:(s,A)\to(r,B)$ compare $C_{B,r}\,h^{-1}D_Y(v)$ and $D_X(v)\,C_{A,s}$. On $[x\otimes a]$ the first map is
$$c_r([q^Y_{s,r}(x)])\otimes\gamma_B([v_Y(a)]),$$
whereas the second is
$$q^X_{s,r}(c_s([x]))\otimes v_X(\gamma_A([a])).$$
The first factors agree by the assumed equation $c_rh^{-1}q^Y_{s,r}=q^X_{s,r}c_s$; the second agree by step 1. The two maps are semilinear over the same coefficient map, so step 3's adjunction and tensor equality test proves the square. Taking $s=r$ proves coefficient naturality, and taking $A=B$, $v=1$ proves exponent naturality, including compatibility with the isomorphism of step 6. Step 4 supplies the diagram laws; step 2 supplies invertible components. Their inverses satisfy the inverse squares by composing this square with the component inverses, so this is an isomorphism of the varying-scalar diagrams.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor

proof.text: Finally use the abelian sheaf tensor structure and its monoidal local equivalences from [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] and [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] on the chosen small sites. These verify the hypotheses for [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison]. Apply the latter over $R_{T,r}$ to $P_{T,r}$ and $A_T$. Its tensor comparison fixes every local pure tensor, and the equivalence fixes underlying abelian sheaves and maps. The extra $A_T$-action is multiplication on the $A_T$ factor; its action on a pure tensor is $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes ba$, and tensor naturality identifies this action in the two interpretations. Consequently the map of step 2 has the same underlying abelian map after internal interpretation: both send $[x\otimes a]$ to $c_r([x])\otimes\gamma_A([a])$, so step 3 proves equality. The identical argument for $x\otimes a\mapsto q_{s,r}(x)\otimes v(a)$ identifies every diagram arrow; hence the squares in step 7 are the same squares on underlying abelian sheaves.
